questions.question: If a 10% increase in the price of good X leads to a 15% decrease in the quantity demanded of good X, what is the absolute price elasticity of demand (E_d), and how is demand classified?
When the income elasticity of demand (E_y) for a commodity is measured to be −0.8, what economic classification does this commodity belong to?
If the cross-price elasticity of demand (E_xy) between two goods, X and Y, is positive (+1.4), how are goods X and Y related in consumption?
A producer faces a perfectly inelastic supply curve (E_s = 0) in the immediate market period. What graphical shape does this supply curve take?

options.A: Horizontal line parallel to the quantity axis
options.B: Vertical line parallel to the price axis
options.C: Upward sloping line passing through the origin

questions.question: If a firm operates along a linear downward-sloping demand curve, at what point along the curve is total revenue (TR) maximized?

options.A: Where price elasticity of demand E_d > 1
options.B: Where price elasticity of demand E_d = 0
options.C: Where price elasticity of demand E_d = 1
options.D: Where price elasticity of demand E_d < 1

questions.question: The market supply function for a commodity is given as Q_s = −20 + 4P. What is the price elasticity of supply when the market price P = ₦10?
When an ad valorem tax is levied on a commodity with relatively price-inelastic demand and price-elastic supply, who bears the larger share of the tax burden?
Which accounting component differentiates Gross National Product (GNP) from Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
Given a closed economy without government intervention, where consumption is C = 100 + 0.75Y and investment is I = 50, what is the equilibrium level of national income (Y)?
If the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) in an economy is 0.80, what is the numerical value of the simple Keynesian investment multiplier (K)?
Which major pitfall must be eliminated when calculating national income via the output (value-added) approach to prevent artificial inflation of GDP figures?

options.C: Exclusion of net foreign trade surplus

questions.question: In the circular flow of income for an open economy, which set of economic variables constitutes injections (J) into the national income stream?
What national accounting identity correctly measures Personal Disposable Income (PDI)?
An economy's Nominal GDP grew by 12% in a given year while Real GDP grew by 4%. What was the approximate percentage rate of inflation as measured by the GDP deflator?
When a central bank conducts Open Market Operations (OMO) by selling government treasury bills to commercial banks, what is the immediate intended policy outcome?

options.A: Increase in commercial bank liquidity and money supply expansion
options.B: Reduction in commercial bank reserves and money supply contraction
options.C: Decrease in the cash reserve ratio (CRR)
options.D: Lowering of the policy discount rate

questions.question: Which monetary policy instrument directly obliges commercial banks to keep a fixed percentage of their total deposit liabilities with the central bank?
To curb demand-pull inflation during an economic boom, which discretionary fiscal policy combination should the government implement?

options.A: Increase government expenditure and decrease tax rates
options.B: Decrease government expenditure and increase tax rates
options.C: Increase central bank bond purchases and reduce interest rates
options.D: Decrease statutory reserve requirements and increase subsidies

questions.question: What type of tax structure is in place when the marginal tax rate increases as an individual's taxable income level rises?
According to Keynesian monetary theory, which motive for holding cash balances is primarily sensitive to changes in interest rates?
When government budget deficits financed by public borrowing lead to higher interest rates that reduce private capital investment, what economic phenomenon occurs?
Which component is classified as an automatic (built-in) fiscal stabilizer during an economic downturn?

options.A: Progressive income tax collections automatically declining
options.B: Central bank lowering the discount rate
options.C: Parliament passing a new infrastructure spending bill

questions.question: In Milton Friedman's Quantity Theory of Money equation MV = PQ, what assumption regarding money velocity (V) and real output (Q) leads monetarists to conclude that money supply changes directly determine price level (P)?

options.A: V and Q are highly volatile in the short run
options.B: V and Q are stable or at full employment capacity in the short run
options.D: P and Q are completely independent of M

questions.question: In a perfectly competitive market, what condition defines profit maximization for an individual firm in both the short run and the long run?
In the long-run equilibrium of a perfectly competitive industry, what economic profit level do existing firms earn due to free entry and exit?
Which market structure is uniquely characterized by mutual interdependence among a few dominant seller firms, often leading to collusive or non-collusive game-theoretic behavior?
The kinked demand curve model proposed by Paul Sweezy explains price rigidity under non-collusive oligopoly. Why is the demand curve inelastic below the prevailing price P*?

options.A: Rival firms will follow price decreases but ignore price increases
options.B: Rival firms will follow price increases but ignore price decreases
options.C: Rival firms will maintain constant production regardless of price
options.D: Consumers become insensitive to price increases

questions.question: A profit-maximizing monopolist practices third-degree price discrimination across two distinct market segments. How does the monopolist set prices in these two markets?

options.A: Higher price in the market with higher price elasticity of demand
options.B: Higher price in the market with lower price elasticity of demand
options.C: Equal prices in both markets regardless of elasticity
options.D: Lower price in the market with lower income level

questions.question: Under monopolistic competition, what key feature differentiates products sold by competing firms in the industry?
A firm operating under perfect competition faces a horizontal demand curve. What does this indicate about the firm's market power?

options.A: The firm is a price maker with complete market power
options.B: The firm is a price taker with zero market power
options.C: The firm can raise price without losing sales volume

questions.question: What is the primary cause of deadweight loss (allocative inefficiency) created by a profit-maximizing pure monopoly?

options.A: Producing where Price equals Marginal Cost (P = MC)
options.B: Producing an output level where Price exceeds Marginal Cost (P > MC)
options.C: Earning normal profits in the long run
options.D: Operating at minimum Average Total Cost (ATC)
